name: Treaty with the Pawnee, 1848 (Grand, Loups, Republicans, etc.)
promises: In return for a tract running from the southern shore of the Platte River north to the crest of the bluffs north of the river, from five miles west of Fort Childs east to the end of Grand Island (supposed to be about sixty miles), the United States paid $2,000 in goods and merchandise on the day of signing (Articles 1 and 2).
The United States also took the privilege of cutting hard timber on Wood River, north of the ceded strip (Article 3).

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission found the Pawnee held original Indian title to the 110,419 acres ceded by this treaty, valued them at $99,380 as of August 6, 1848, held that the $2,000 in goods paid for them was an unconscionable consideration, and awarded $97,380 (Claim III), carried into the final award of July 6, 1962.

landTaken: 110,419 acres along the Platte River, from its southern shore north to the bluffs, which the Commission found the Pawnee held by original Indian title (Docket 10, Interlocutory Order, June 17, 1957), worth $99,380 or an average of ninety cents an acre in 1848.
compensation: $2,000 in goods paid at signing. The Commission awarded $97,380 for this cession (Third Interlocutory Order, June 14, 1960), part of the Pawnee final award of $7,315,985.70 (July 6, 1962).
today: The claimant was the Pawnee Indian Tribe of Oklahoma, consisting of the four confederated bands. The other Pawnee cessions in the same docket are kappler-424 (1833) and kappler-772 (1857).

nationVoice.summary: The Nation's Pawnee Portal presents its treaties of 1818 to 1857 as binding agreements between sovereign nations, covering peace, trade, land cessions, assimilation programs and annuities, and records that the 1848 treaty was made at Fort Childs near the head of Grand Island, on the south side of the Platte River.

openQuestions: The OCR of finding 107 reads the value once as $39,380 and once as $99,380; $99,380 is consistent with the $97,380 award (value less the $2,000 paid) and with the ninety cents an acre the finding states.
The Pawnee Nation's website was locked to automated readers in this pass, so its own account is not linked yet.

Audit 2026-11-08: the ceded tract was described as south of the Platte; Article 1 runs from the southern shore of the Platte north to the crest of the bluffs north of the river, so promise 1 and landTaken were corrected. ICC figures ($99,380, $97,380, $7,315,985.70, 110,419 acres) held; finding 107 does print $39,380 once and finding 108 prints $99,380.
